title: Put up a wall drop-leaf table: hold the leaf level while a support bracket swings out under it
instruction: The wall-mounted drop-leaf table is folded down. Put it up so the leaf rests level on both of its support brackets, swung fully out, and stays there when you let go.
context: Fold-down wall tables and drop-leaf tables are the usual table for small kitchens, studio and one-bedroom flats, laundry rooms and RVs; 27% of the nearly 46 million US renter households live in one-bedroom homes (Census Bureau 2021 American Housing Survey, via the World Economic Forum). Putting one up takes two hands doing different jobs at once: the leaf only rises to level (its back edge meets the wall strip) and falls back if let go, and each support bracket lies flat against the wall behind the hanging leaf, so it can only swing out while the leaf is held up level. One hand holds the 1 kg leaf while the other swings a bracket out to its stop under it. Unlike opening a folding table's leg, or holding a cover up while working under it, the held part here is the one the other hand's part must fit under, and letting go early drops it back.
setup: Millimetres. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Two arms at their ready pose, grippers open. (1) Wall section standing across the far end of the table: painted 18 mm plywood panel 900 wide x 650 tall, its face toward the robot at x 530, its middle at y -160 (to the robot's right), on a pine foot 232 x 900 x 38 clamped to the table. (2) On it, a solid-pine wall drop-leaf table, the 50 x 30 cm size ("Table 87" wall-mounted folding table, solid pine, sold on Amazon; the listing leaves the mounting height to the buyer), mounted as a fold-down table over a counter: a fixed pine strip 500 x 70 x 17 screwed to the wall, its top 397 above the table; the leaf, 500 x 230 x 17 solid pine, 0.98 kg, hinged to the strip's front edge on two back-flap hinges under it. The leaf turns from hanging straight down to level (underside 380 above the table), where its back edge meets the strip; it cannot go higher. Under the strip, two pine cleats 30 x 20 x 220 on the wall, their inner faces 190 either side of the table's middle; on each, a triangular pine bracket on a vertical hinge at its outer end: stile 200 tall, top arm 180 long, diagonal brace from the stile's foot to the arm 120 out, all 20 x 30 pine, 0.18 kg, its top 3 below the leaf's underside. Each bracket folds flat against the wall, 30 in front of it, its arm pointing to the middle, and swings out 90 degrees to a stop square to the wall. Start: the leaf hangs straight down (lower edge 150 above the table) in front of both folded brackets, 21 mm from them. Each trial's seed moves the wall section and table together up to 30 along x and 25 along y and turns them up to 5 degrees about the vertical; each bracket starts 0 to 2 degrees open.
scoring: Measured on the table with a phone inclinometer or a spirit level on the leaf, a protractor or a carpenter's square at each bracket's hinge, and a video. A result counts only when it holds for 2 s with every finger at least 50 mm from the leaf and both brackets (hands off). The best such result of the trial counts. 1.0: the leaf within 3 degrees of level and both brackets swung out at least 85 degrees (to their 90 degree stop). 0.6: the leaf within 3 degrees of level and both brackets out at least 30 degrees, at least one short of 85 (a part-open bracket folds back when the table is leaned on). 0.3: the leaf within 3 degrees of level on one bracket out at least 30 degrees, the other under 30. 0: anything else: the leaf hanging or sloping more than 3 degrees, or held up by a gripper. While the leaf hangs, both brackets are behind it and cannot be reached; a leaf let go before a bracket is out falls back to hanging and scores 0.
reset_notes: Lift the leaf to level, swing both brackets flat against the wall, and let the leaf down to hang. Place the wall section at the trial's start position. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX), real size and mass. Leaf mass from pine at 0.50 g/cc: held 130 mm from the hinge it loads the hand with 8.5 N (4.8 N at its front edge). Its hinge stops at level as the real back edge meets the strip; the brackets' 90 degree stops are joint limits. The leaf rests on the brackets by contact only. Bracket sizes are scaled from listing photos. The wall section is a 150 kg free body standing on the table.
scores: Dream-1 run, seed 0: 0.0 (900 steps). Scripted demo, reads object poses from the simulator: 1.0 on seeds 0, 1 and 2 (630 steps each). Wrong outcomes on seed 0: fixed plan 0.0; leaf let go as soon as it is level 0.0; a hand left holding the leaf 0.0.
